# gsDesignNB

> Sample size, simulation, and group sequential design for clinical trials with negative binomial recurrent event endpoints.

gsDesignNB is an R package for planning, monitoring, and adapting clinical trials whose primary endpoint is a recurrent event count analyzed with a negative binomial model. It extends the gsDesign ecosystem to handle information that depends on exposure and dispersion, protocol event gaps, calendar-time interim looks, and blinded/unblinded sample size re-estimation.

## Key links

- Documentation: https://keaven.github.io/gsDesignNB/
- Repository: https://github.com/keaven/gsDesignNB
- Bug reports: https://github.com/keaven/gsDesignNB/issues
- AI skill file: https://github.com/keaven/gsDesignNB/blob/main/SKILL.md

## Core functions

- `sample_size_nbinom()`: Sample size (or power) for comparing two NB groups. Supports Wald and score test sizing, variable accrual, dropout, max follow-up, event gaps with Jensen correction, and non-inferiority/super-superiority margins.
- `mutze_test()`: Wald or score test for treatment effect from aggregated subject-level data. Auto-fallback to Poisson or method-of-moments when ML fit is unreliable.
- `nb_sim()`: Simulate recurrent-event trial data with piecewise accrual, dropout, and maximum follow-up.
- `nb_sim_seasonal()`: Simulate with time-varying (seasonal) event rates.
- `gsNBCalendar()`: Calendar-time group sequential design for NB outcomes, building on gsDesign.
- `sim_gs_nbinom()`: Monte Carlo simulation of group sequential NB trials.
- `blinded_ssr()`: Blinded sample size re-estimation from pooled interim data.
- `unblinded_ssr()`: Unblinded SSR using treatment-specific interim estimates.
- `calculate_blinded_info()`: Estimate statistical information from blinded interim data.
- `compute_info_at_time()`: Compute expected information at a given analysis time.
- `cut_data_by_date()`: Truncate simulated data at a calendar date for interim analysis.
- `cut_completers()`: Cut data to include only patients who completed follow-up.
- `estimate_nb_mom()`: Method-of-moments estimation of NB dispersion from blinded data.
- `impute_nb_mar()`: Multiple imputation under missing-at-random for NB outcomes.
- `impute_nb_composite()`: Composite imputation combining MAR and reference-based patterns.

## Statistical model

Events follow a Gamma-Poisson mixture: Var(Y) = μ + kμ², where k is the dispersion parameter and μ = λt (rate × exposure). The treatment effect is the log rate ratio θ = log(λ₂/λ₁). Fisher information per subject: I = μ/(1 + kμ).

## Disease-area parameter ranges

- COPD exacerbations: 0.5–1.5 events/year, k ∈ [0.5, 1.0], often with 28-day event gap
- Heart failure hospitalizations: ~0.3 events/month, k ≈ 0.5
- MS relapses: 0.3–1.5 events/year, moderate-to-high k

## Dispersion conventions

This package uses Var = μ + kμ² (k = dispersion). Other conventions in the literature:
- Friede & Schmidli (2010): φ = k (same as ours)
- Mutze et al. (2019): κ = 1/k (inverse — the Gamma shape parameter)
- R's rnbinom(): size = 1/k
